title: Late Breaking Results: Efficient Built-in Self-Test for Microfluidic Large-Scale Integration (mLSI)
problem: Microfluidic LSI chips have n control channels susceptible to blockage and leakage defects. Traditional exhaustive testing requires a large number of test patterns to validate all channels.
motivation: Efficient testing methodology is critical for microfluidic chip manufacturing and yield improvement as device complexity scales.
method: A graph theory-based BIST approach minimizes test patterns using control channel topology. Blockage tests reduce from exponential patterns to 1. Leakage tests reduce from ⌈log2(n + 1)⌉ to ⌈log2(χ(G) + 1)⌉ patterns by applying vertex chromatic number χ(G) of the control channel graph.
key_novelty: Using graph vertex coloring to dramatically reduce leakage test patterns in microfluidic BIST design.
contributions: BIST method reducing blockage test patterns to 1 independent of channel count
Graph chromatic number-based reduction of leakage test patterns from linear to logarithmic complexity
Fabricated implementation demonstrating practical feasibility of the approach
Drastic improvement in overall test efficiency for microfluidic LSI chips

metrics.other: blockage test patterns reduced to 1; leakage test patterns reduced from log2(n+1) to log2(chromatic_number+1)
